newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Comm Bank aims to boost 97/98 profits.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Comm Bank aims to boost 97/98 profits.

text.p: Commonweath Bank of Australia said on Tuesday it would aim to improve profits in the year to June 30, 1998, but that it was too early to make a specific prediction.

Commonwealth Bank managing director David Murray told reporters the bank aimed to achieve higher profits in 1997/98, despite the bank's prediction that profits would be flat in the current 1996/97 year.
Murray was asked if the bank aimed to increase profits in the 1997/98 year after flat profits this financial year.
"Yes," he said. "It means marketing better and containing our costs," he added.
Earlier, CBA chairman Tim Besley told the bank's annual meeting he saw increased competition in the banking sector, forcing banking industry profits to fall over the longer term.
"We have to be sure that ours come down as little as any of the others," Besley said.
However, Murray later clarified Besley's comments, saying he was referring to a fall in profit growth rates in the future.
"I read that comment to mean a fall in the growth rate in profits," he said.

Murray again repeated that the bank's pre-emptive cut of its variable home loan rates in the mid-1996, combined with the interest costs linked to the CBA's buy-back of government shares, would lead to flat profits overall in 1996/97.
